rules.title: Wire keys are camelCase, both directions
rules.trigger: an aggregate with a multi-word field (`commitSha: string`) on create/update
rules.observable: POST {"commitSha":…} persists commit_sha and reads back {"commitSha":…}; a multi-word field is never silently dropped to a 422

rules.title: Enum values use declared casing on the wire
rules.trigger: enum BuildState = Passed | Failed; a field of that type on a create body

rules.title: No persistence-internal columns leak to the wire
rules.trigger: any read of a softDeletable/auditable aggregate, or an ORM that auto-stamps timestamps
rules.observable: GET returns exactly the wireShape keys — no inserted_at/updated_at, no internal jsonb envelope

rules.title: Declared temporal fields round-trip
rules.trigger: an aggregate declaring `createdAt: instant` with an explicit create
rules.observable: POST {"createdAt":"2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"} reads back the same instant (ORM auto-value does not clobber it)

rules.title: Union-variant absence match is a presence check everywhere
rules.trigger: `find one X or absent` feeding a match { X => … | absent => … }
rules.observable: the absent arm is taken when the row is missing, identically across backends (nullable-subject ternary)

rules.title: Boolean create defaults materialize at the wire boundary
rules.trigger: `active: bool = true`; a create body omitting `active`
rules.observable: POST {} (no active) reads back {"active":true}, not a zero-value false/null

rules.title: Value-object subfields survive a jsonb round-trip
rules.trigger: valueobject Money { amount, currency } as an aggregate field on a jsonb-storing backend
rules.observable: GET returns the nested {amount,currency}; a later op reading self.price.amount does not raise

rules.title: Associations persist and preload on round-trip
rules.trigger: an op mutating a containment or X id[] ref-collection (`lines += …`, `members += t`)
rules.observable: after the op, GET nests the added child / lists the added id — no in-memory projection that omits the join write

rules.title: Error bodies converge on RFC 7807 with the 400/422 split
rules.trigger: a create violating an invariant vs a create with a malformed body
rules.observable: malformed body → 400, well-formed-but-invalid → 422; identical problem-body shape on every backend

rules.title: Rehydration trusts the store — invariants guard transitions only
rules.trigger: an aggregate with an invariant; a persisted row that predates a tightened invariant is read back
rules.observable: GET/findAll return the stored row (no invariant re-run on load), so it can be repaired via an operation; create and every mutator still assert

rules.title: A created `versioned` aggregate reads back at version 1
rules.trigger: a `versioned` aggregate created via POST, then read back
rules.observable: the optimistic-concurrency `version` on the first read is 1 — the `versioned` capability declares `version: int token = 1` (src/macros/prelude.ts), mirrored to `version INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1`. All five backends honor it: node stamps it in its versioned save, elixir carries the Ecto `default: 1`, and dotnet/java/python seed it in the domain `create` factory (`constructionSeededDefaults`) since a `token` field is dropped from the create body.
provenance: pinned per-PR by the wire-golden gate (payments)

rules.title: Money wire scale is consistent across backends
rules.trigger: a money-typed field serialized to the wire (e.g. `costFloor`)
rules.observable: a money-typed field serializes at a FIXED scale of 4 on every backend — the canonical NUMERIC(19,4) storage scale (`MONEY_WIRE_SCALE`, src/generator/money-scale.ts). `12.5`, `12.50` and `12` all read back as `"12.5000"`, stored or derived. Each backend formats at the wire boundary: node `.toFixed(4)`, .NET `ToString("F4")`, Java `setScale(4, HALF_UP)`, Python `quantize(1e-4, ROUND_HALF_UP)`, Elixir `__money_round/1`.

rules.title: A create POST returns the id envelope, not the whole aggregate
rules.observable: the 201 body is the id envelope `{"id": …}` and nothing else. Elixir instead returns the FULL aggregate (`{"id":…,"owner":"alice","balance":0}`), so a client written against the declared create response reads fields on one backend it cannot read on the other four — and every declared-but-unreturned field is a silent contract break the OpenAPI spec-diff cannot see (the spec agrees; only the BYTES differ).
provenance: elixir `create_result/2` json(serialize(record)) vs the emitted Create<Agg>Response `{id}` schema (openapi-emit.ts)

rules.title: `version` increments on every persisted mutation, document shapes included
rules.trigger: a `versioned` aggregate with `shape: document` (jsonb-stored): create, invoke an operation, read back
rules.observable: the optimistic-concurrency `version` reads back 1 + one per persisted mutation, for EVERY `shape:`. node and python do. The other three each drop the bump on a DIFFERENT shape, which is why no single fixture caught it — document `Cart` / embedded `Wishlist` / plain `Order` (2 / 2 / 3 canonical) read back 1 / 2 / 3 on dotnet+java and 2 / 1 / 1 on elixir. dotnet/java: the ORM concurrency token is bound to a mapped column and a document aggregate's `version` lives inside the jsonb blob — the `dapper` persistence adapter (raw Npgsql, same .NET emitters, hand-rolled document SQL) increments correctly, which localizes the gap to the EF/JPA mapping rather than the .NET/Java wire emitters. elixir: the mirror image — the document path bumps, but an operation on an embedded/plain aggregate persists without touching `version` at all.
